## Note on my evidence base (read once, applies to everything below)

I answer from a single surviving retention file, reader 23's notes, which is the terminal node of a
hand-off chain that was truncated at line 800 at every hop. What I hold:

- **R24 (Orra Keddie's diary, published 1964) quoted in full** — preface, all entries, the loose 1934 leaf.
- **Everything else only as summary, tabulation and quoted fragment.** The full texts of **R19 (the
  Chronicle, 1958), R20 (Junia Ammon's firm history, 1949), R22 (Orin Falke's 1959 county report) and
  R23 (Bertram Kyle's 1953 memoir)** were written up by earlier readers and were cut out of the hand-offs.
  Two named sections — Kyle's "five and a quarter per cent" and something the chain called "the
  arithmetic lock" — were lost entire.
- I never saw r01–r03, r05–r07, r09–r11, r14 in any form.

So where I say "the sources say," I mean "the chain's tabulation of the sources says." I flag every
place where that distinction could change the answer.

I was also not told which six stories Batches 1 and 2 covered. The eight-story set is not listed
anywhere in my notes. **I infer** from the case chronology that the six already asked about are:
(1) the founding of the Association and the opening of the Ostrey Hollow skimming station, 1896;
(2) the buying of the station's own glass from Junia Ammon's firm, 1897; (3) the long grievance and
the 1908 hay committee; (4) the 1911 breakage and the nine weeks on borrowed glass; (5) the 1919
water circular and the Keddie–Emmet break; (6) the 1923 condemnation and the crate in the loft.
That leaves **the 1925 arbitration and dismissal**, and **the vindication of 1934–1981**, as the last
two in order of occurrence. Those are the two I reconstruct.
